papers.title: Resident tissue macrophages transfer selenium transporter protein to protect pancreatic cancer from ferroptosis.
papers.summary: Resident tissue macrophages localize at pancreatic cancer borders and transfer the selenium transporter SELENOP to EMT-high tumor cells via LRP8 uptake. Raised selenium limits lipid peroxidation and shields cells from ferroptosis; macrophage SELENOP deletion or LRP8 disruption reduced EMT and progression, with a conserved border niche seen in human PDAC.

papers.title: Shifts in embryonic oxygen levels cue heterochrony in limb initiation.
papers.summary: Mammalian limb heterochrony — delayed hindlimb relative to forelimb development — is evident from limb bud onset and tied to heterochronic T-box transcription factor expression. Unexpectedly, this shift is not cis-regulatory but driven by differing embryonic oxygen environments, mediated through the NF-kappaB family factor cRel and hypoxia-sensing HIF1alpha.

papers.title: Ceramide synthesis mediates colorectal cancer metastasis through a YAP-driven regenerative program.
papers.summary: Dietary fat amplifies tumor-intrinsic DEGS1-mediated de novo ceramide synthesis in colorectal cancer. Ceramide activates YAP through PP2A dephosphorylation, driving a durable BASP1-marked regenerative program that initiates metastasis. DEGS1 loss reduced metastasis without affecting primary tumor growth, and eliminating BASP1-high cells prevented metastatic seeding.

papers.title: Senescence-directed nanotherapy ameliorates fibrosis and overcomes immune exclusion in cancer.
papers.summary: P-selectin marks pathogenic senescent-like cells in fibrotic tissues and tumors. Fucoidan-based senescence-modulating nanoparticles targeting P-selectin showed antifibrotic and immunomodulatory effects, targeting immunosuppressive macrophages. In fibrotic tumors, niche remodeling restored immune infiltration and sensitized tumors to immune checkpoint therapies, offering a generalizable senescence-directed strategy.

papers.title: Escape of the BC200 gene to a human poxvirus reveals its persistent transposition in primates.
papers.summary: The human BC200 noncoding RNA gene was captured twice by the poxvirus molluscum contagiosum virus via L1-mediated retrotransposition in modern human history. BC200 served as a master source of germline retrotransposition throughout anthropoid evolution, spawning hundreds of insertions and still producing polymorphisms, blurring the gene-transposon boundary.

papers.title: Mammals produce cyclo-octasulfur to suppress lipid peroxidation and ferroptosis.
papers.summary: Mammals harbor elemental sulfur as cyclo-octasulfur (S8), accumulating to millimolar levels in mitochondrial membranes and lipid droplets. Lipid droplet-associated nitric oxide synthase drives S8 biosynthesis, and S8 limits lipid peroxidation and suppresses ferroptosis; solubilized S8 injection reduced peroxidation in a mouse osteoarthritis model.

papers.title: Targeting an atypical G protein-coupled receptor signaling pathway for cardiac fibrosis therapy.
papers.summary: Using an iPSC-based discovery platform, CGS15943 emerged as a lead antifibrotic validated in human cardiac fibroblasts, engineered heart tissues, and heart failure models. It suppresses an atypical adenosine receptor pathway where receptor subtypes converge on G-beta-gamma to activate PI3K-AKT and YAP, establishing a targetable fibrosis axis.

papers.title: Fibroblasts restrain gut inflammation by IGF1-dependent regulation of innate lymphocytes.
papers.summary: IGF1-expressing fibroblasts, reduced in inflammatory bowel disease patients, restrain gut inflammation by limiting CXCL10 production by group 3 innate lymphoid cells, thereby reducing plasmacytoid dendritic cell recruitment. Mouse models and conserved human ILC3 biology support an anti-inflammatory fibroblast-ILC3-pDC axis that may fail in IBD.

papers.title: Systemic delivery of phagocytosis-shielded retroviral vectors enables in vivo HSC gene therapy for sickle cell disease.
papers.summary: Phagocytosis-shielded BAEvRless-pseudotyped retroviral vectors enable in vivo HSC gene transfer in humanized mice: up to 8.8% gene marking, enrichable to 70% of CD45+ cells, with stable polyclonal reconstitution. For sickle cell disease, erythroid-specific BCL11A/ZNF410 silencing derepressed gamma-globin to 61.5% of beta-like globins.

papers.title: Immunoids: Building immunocompetent organoids from human pluripotent stem cells.
papers.summary: Immunoids — pluripotent stem cell-derived immunocompetent organoids and assembloids — now span immune incorporation across organ systems, multilineage differentiation, and endogenous immune co-development. This perspective reviews platform advances, argues fabrication standards are needed for physiological modeling, and positions immunoids as future precision-medicine cornerstones for development, disease, and therapy studies.

papers.title: Simplifying in silico protein evolution with minimal screening by unZipro.
papers.summary: unZipro couples a compact inverse-folding protein model with meta-learning to derive family-specific fitness landscapes, enabling zero-shot in silico protein evolution. From minimal ~10-candidate libraries it achieved 61% average success across nine proteins, including a 28-fold activity gain for T5E-CasPhi2 variants and improved plant gene-editing nucleases.

papers.title: DNA methylation: unifying framework for complex chronic conditions.
papers.summary: This review proposes DNA methylation as a unifying epigenetic framework for myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome, long covid, fibromyalgia, and hypermobile Ehlers-Danlos syndrome — overlapping conditions with unclear mechanisms. Cross-condition comparative and longitudinal methylation studies could advance mechanistic insight, diagnostic stratification, and patient outcomes.

papers.title: Natural selection shapes the evolution of the metabolome in Saccharomyces cerevisiae.
papers.summary: Quantifying 1,037 metabolites across Saccharomyces cerevisiae mutation accumulation lines and wild isolates shows metabolite abundances are strongly conserved among wild strains despite ~40-fold genomic divergence, indicating pervasive selection. Roughly 29% of metabolites show directional selection favoring high-abundance species, while amino acids were preferentially driven downward, likely reflecting biosynthetic energy costs.

papers.title: Matrix viscoelasticity amplifies pro-fibrotic crosstalk between cardiac fibroblasts and macrophages.
papers.summary: A viscoelastic coculture platform reveals tissue mechanics regulate cardiac fibroblast-macrophage crosstalk: soft, viscous matrices promote fibroblast activation and healing-polarized macrophages and amplify pro-fibrotic signaling. A STAT1/AP-1-driven feedback loop involving IL6, CCL5, CCL2, VEGFA, and CTGF underlies amplification, establishing viscoelasticity as a central fibrosis regulator.

papers.title: Peptide-mediated CRISPR delivery: From dish to bloodstream.
papers.summary: This review evaluates peptide-mediated CRISPR delivery as a tunable, non-viral alternative to viral vectors and lipid nanoparticles. Peptide platforms compete with electroporation in culture, but in vivo translation faces tissue and systemic barriers — hepatic clearance, phagocytic capture, protein corona — and must integrate chemical innovations into single robust vehicles.

papers.title: Variants in TREX complex subunits (THOC2, ALYREF, THOC6, THOC7) define a neurodevelopmental disability spectrum.
papers.journal: Genetics in medicine : official journal of the American College of Medical Genetics
papers.summary: Aggregating 40 individuals with variants in TREX complex subunits THOC2, ALYREF, THOC6, and THOC7 defines a TREX spectrum neurodevelopmental disorder. Variants are generally partial loss-of-function, altering protein localization, stability, or interactions, with consistent DNA damage accumulation; cognitive, speech, respiratory, and facial dysmorphism features recur across subunits.

papers.title: Advances in bioelectrical sensing and signal transduction.
papers.summary: Reviewing bioelectrical signaling in embryogenesis and regeneration: non-neural cells generate electrical currents whose tissue-level interplay creates endogenous electric fields. Cells sense and transduce these landscapes into directed migration, growth, and differentiation. The authors argue current models of morphogenesis remain incomplete without integrating bioelectrical signals alongside molecular and mechanical frameworks.

papers.title: Mechanistic insights into the inhibition of insulin amyloidogenesis and associated toxicity by the p.M14L variant of exenatide.
papers.summary: The p.M14L exenatide variant acts as a chaperone-like inhibitor of insulin amyloidogenesis, redirecting aggregation from mature fibrils toward off-pathway amorphous aggregates with smaller hydrodynamic diameters. Spectroscopy, AFM/DLS, simulations, and SH-SY5Y cell assays show reduced cytotoxicity and apoptosis, suggesting formulation-stability and anti-amyloid therapeutic potential.

papers.title: The molecular interplay between USP32 and ERP44 in driving multiple myeloma progression and tumor growth.
papers.summary: In multiple myeloma, high ERP44 expression correlates with poor prognosis and promotes proliferation. USP32 stabilizes ERP44 through deubiquitination; ERP44 activates PI3K-AKT signaling, upregulating CDK2 and cyclin D1, plus unfolded protein response markers and osteolytic factors. The USP32-ERP44-PI3K/AKT axis emerges as a pro-tumor regulatory pathway.

papers.title: A knockin Ntsr1(Flp) driver enables intersectional and systemic targeting of heterogeneous midbrain dopamine circuits.
papers.summary: A knockin Ntsr1-Flp driver mouse enables intersectional targeting of NTSR1-expressing neurons, revealing midbrain populations include both dopaminergic and non-dopaminergic neurons. Complementary dual-recombinase reporter configurations showed configuration-dependent dopamine targeting, and Flp/Cre-dependent tACaspase-3 enabled selective ablation, establishing Ntsr1-Flp for scalable Boolean circuit analysis.

papers.title: A single-cell spatiotemporal manifold of tissue morphology and dynamics.
papers.summary: A transformer-based embedding of cell point clouds over time yields a single-cell spatiotemporal manifold capturing tissue morphology and dynamics. Embeddings show interpretable cell-type clusters, preserved local distances, and a pseudo-time axis, enabling anatomical annotation at cellular resolution and detection of subtle, transient phenotypes in large screens.

papers.title: Duration-dependent mild heat stress attenuates mercury-induced Neuroreproductive and oxidative toxicity in Drosophila melanogaster via hormetic mechanisms.
papers.journal: Biometals : an international journal on the role of metal ions in biology, biochemistry, and medicine
papers.summary: In Drosophila, brief (5-minute) mild heat stress hormetically attenuates mercury chloride toxicity, improving survival, locomotion, fecundity, redox balance, dopamine levels, and brain architecture, partly via restored thiol status and ATPase activity. Longer (15-minute) exposure gave limited protection and was mildly harmful itself, demonstrating duration-dependent hormesis.

papers.title: Role of the m6A methyltransferase Mettl16 in Drosophila development.
papers.summary: Unlike in mammals, Drosophila Mettl16 mutants are viable but sterile with severe gametogenesis defects. METTL16 deposits m6A on a small transcript subset — contrasting METTL3's broad effects — interacts with and methylates U6 snRNA, and its loss causes widespread alternative splicing changes, explaining the pleiotropic developmental phenotypes.

papers.title: Postnatal heart development is coordinated by multi-lineage Wnt and BMP signaling.
papers.summary: Neonatal mouse heart analysis shows the proliferation-to-enlargement transition occurs between postnatal days 3.5-4.5, with declining beta-catenin and rising SMAD1/5/9 phosphorylation. Disrupting beta-catenin/CBP promotes cardiomyocyte enlargement while stabilization enhances proliferation; Wnt is active across endothelial, mesenchymal, and neural lineages, with BMP peaking in cardiomyocytes at P6.

papers.title: Phytoestrogens and related microbial metabolites remodel aberrant prostate transcriptomic profiles generated upon exposure to oxidative stress.
papers.summary: In hydrogen peroxide-challenged human prostate epithelial cells, RNA-seq with a weighted recovery ratio metric shows the pterostilbene microbial metabolite pinostilbene recovered 69% of stress-responsive genes and pterostilbene 47%, versus only 9% for genistein. PTS and PNS, but not GEN, restored DNA methylation-related genes, indicating structure-dependent phytoestrogen actions.

papers.title: Mapping of Metabolic Glycan Labeling Tolerance Based on SERS-Imaging of N-Substituted Unnatural Sugar Analogs in the Hexosamine Biosynthetic Pathway.
papers.summary: Using metabolic glycan labeling with SERS imaging, this study maps hexosamine biosynthetic pathway tolerance for N-substituted mannosamine and glucosamine analogs. ManNAcPhalk showed the highest cell-surface glycan labeling efficiency; all analogs predominantly labeled N-glycans, validated by far-western blotting, guiding design of unnatural sugars for glycan tracking and diagnostics.

papers.title: Targeted Control of Protein O-GlcNAcylation in Living Cells.
papers.summary: Review of protein-selective O-GlcNAcylation control in living cells: small-molecule recruiters, nanobody systems, inducible recruitment, and RNA aptamers direct OGT or OGA to chosen substrates. The authors compare what each approach can establish and required controls — target engagement, site assignment, selectivity — for assigning phenotypes to specific substrates.

papers.title: Molecular characterization of the type 2 diabetes-associated interleukin-6 receptor single nucleotide polymorphism p.V385I (rs2228146).
papers.summary: The type 2 diabetes-associated IL-6R variant p.V385I (rs2228146) lies within the transmembrane helix. The receptor matures and reaches the cell surface at wild-type levels, is cleavable by ADAM10/ADAM17 to generate soluble IL-6R, and retains classic signaling, distinguishing it mechanistically from the rs2228145 variant.

papers.title: In situ visualization of autophagy reveals the presence of vesicles at the expanding phagophore rim.
papers.summary: Using an ATG2 variant that slows autophagosome biogenesis, cryo-correlative light and electron microscopy and in situ cryo-electron tomography in yeast reveal enlarged, vesicle-surrounded phagophore rims. Vesicle dimensions and attachments are consistent with cytosolic vesicle fusion, showing fusion contributes to phagophore expansion beyond the initial nucleation phase.

papers.title: In silico engineering fibrin-directed streptokinase - kringle 2 fusion: Structural insights into fibrin interaction and plasminogen recognition.
papers.summary: Computational design of a streptokinase C-terminal fusion with tissue plasminogen activator kringle 2 shows high-confidence fibrin interactions and more favorable predicted fibrin binding than native streptokinase, without losing predicted plasminogen binding. Docking convergence identifies residue Arg515 as a priority for experimental evaluation of clot-directed fibrinolysis.

papers.title: Characterizing two nanobodies for SMAD4.
papers.summary: Two nanobodies targeting the SMAD4-MH2 domain with high affinity show distinct, overlapping epitopes. NBS4A1 blocks SMAD4 binding to R-SMADs while NBS4A7 recognizes SMAD4 even when R-SMAD-bound, enabling structural and cellular study of folded SMAD complexes with cofactors or DNA in different experimental contexts.

papers.title: Loss-Of-Function CCM Gene Variants in Japanese Patients With Cerebral Cavernous Malformations.
papers.summary: Sequencing 11 Japanese familial cerebral cavernous malformation patients identified heterozygous loss-of-function variants across KRIT1, CCM2, and PDCD10, including two non-canonical splice variants confirmed by in vitro splicing assays. One heavily lesioned patient showed no variants at known loci, suggesting either bioinformatic limitations or a novel CCM gene.

papers.title: Shared genetic architecture of HCM and AF: Elevated NPPA/ANP is linked to atrial electrical remodeling.
papers.summary: Integrating databases and network analysis identifies 11 shared genes between hypertrophic cardiomyopathy and atrial fibrillation, with NPPA, ACE, and POMC as hubs. NT-proANP serum levels were elevated in HCM and higher still with AF, supporting NPPA/ANP-driven atrial electrical remodeling as a mechanistic link.

papers.title: Proteome-wide remodelling in Klebsiella pneumoniae during step-wise adaptive evolution against colistin.
papers.summary: Short-duration colistin exposure in Klebsiella pneumoniae produced an ~8-fold MIC increase at 1x MIC alone — a nonlinear adaptive response. Proteomics of 1,379 proteins revealed a core signature including LPS modification (ArnA, ArnB) and metabolic reprogramming of carbon/amino acid metabolism and translation machinery, illuminating early resistance emergence.

papers.title: Transcriptomic associations and biomarkers in ANCA‑associated Glomerulonephritis and IgG4‑related Disease: A bioinformatics and machine learning study.
papers.summary: Cross-tissue transcriptomic comparison of ANCA-associated glomerulonephritis and IgG4-related disease identified 305 differentially expressed genes and candidate shared markers. ITGAM showed robust predictive performance in internal and external validation (AUC 0.921/0.844), while CXCL1 generalized poorly, establishing ITGAM as the more reliable cross-disease biomarker candidate.

papers.title: Physicochemical and biological properties of three calcium silicate-based root canal sealers.
papers.summary: Comparing three calcium silicate root canal sealers: proroot MTA and MTA Plus released more calcium and promoted mineralization, while Bio C Sealer and BioRoot RCS showed higher solubility and concentration-dependent cytotoxicity. BioRoot increased MMP-1 secretion via p38, JNK, and ERK1/2 MAPK activation, with caveats from in vitro conditions.

papers.title: Proteomic machine-learning signatures associated with carotid plaque: A population-based hypothesis-generating study.
papers.summary: In 693 population-based participants profiled with 460 Olink proteins, a Boruta/random-forest pipeline identified 42 carotid plaque biomarkers — led by GDF-15, CDCP1, CHIT1, FLT3LG, CDH2, and CRTAC1 — and a 25-marker machine-learning fingerprint with good internal cross-validation. Results are hypothesis-generating pending prospective external validation.

papers.title: Waterpipe smoke condensate activates autophagy in non-tumorigenic lung epithelial cells: Implications for inflammation and stemness.
papers.summary: Waterpipe smoke condensate in non-tumorigenic bronchial epithelial cells activates autophagy — LC3-II and p62 accumulation, AMPK activation, mTORC1 inhibition — which is protective since bafilomycin A1 increased cell death. Exposure also induced DNA damage (gamma-H2AX, 53BP1), inflammatory cytokines, and cancer stemness markers CD44/CD133, linking waterpipe smoke to early carcinogenesis events.

papers.title: Azithromycin and its non-antibacterial derivative EP317 attenuate select aspects of ventilator-induced lung injury in rats.
papers.summary: In rat ventilator-induced lung injury, both azithromycin and its non-antibacterial derivative EP317 attenuated pulmonary edema, improved survival, and reduced plasma inflammatory cytokines, though bronchoalveolar protein levels were unchanged. EP317 retains the immunomodulatory and barrier-strengthening benefits while avoiding antibacterial resistance concerns of macrolides.

papers.title: Resmetirom attenuates atherosclerosis-associated dyslipidemia and vascular inflammation in high-fat diet-fed ApoE-/- mice.
papers.summary: The liver-targeted THR-beta agonist resmetirom in ApoE-/- mice dose-dependently reduced aortic plaque burden and atherogenic dyslipidemia — high dose lowered LDL-C 39.5% — while suppressing NLRP3/caspase-1, IL-1beta (-59%), NF-kappaB signaling, ROS, and the M1/M2 macrophage ratio (-73%), showing combined lipid-lowering and vascular anti-inflammatory actions.

papers.title: M2-Exo-derived miR-1227-5p protects against periodontitis through inhibiting USP2-dependent deubiquitination of Drp1.
papers.summary: M2 macrophage-derived exosomal miR-1227-5p protects against periodontitis by directly targeting USP2, inhibiting USP2-dependent deubiquitination of Drp1. In a ligusticum-exposed periodontal ligament stem cell model, the miRNA improved mitochondrial function and promoted proliferation and osteogenesis, positioning M2 exosomes as candidate therapeutics.

papers.title: Integrated bioinformatics analysis, machine learning, and experimental validation reveal that ACSL1 drives myocardial ischemia reperfusion injury via ferroptosis.
papers.summary: Integrating GEO datasets with three machine-learning algorithms identifies ACSL1 as the characteristic ferroptosis-related gene in myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury. FOXO4 transcriptionally regulates ACSL1 (validated by reporter and ChIP assays), TRIM25 stabilizes it, and ACSL1 drives ferroptotic myocardial injury in a mouse model, marking it as a therapeutic candidate.

papers.title: Deletion of the mouse myocardial Nppb gene alleviates sepsis-induced myocardial dysfunction.
papers.summary: Cardiac-specific Nppb conditional knockout mice challenged with sepsis showed preserved contractility, less structural damage, suppressed endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition, restored NOTCH1 signaling, and improved survival. Deletion of the BNP-encoding gene protects against sepsis-induced myocardial dysfunction, suggesting NPPB inhibition as a potential strategy for septic cardiomyopathy.

papers.title: Protective and therapeutic roles of Phoenix dactylifera L. Zaghloul cultivar leaves extract against ethanol-induced gastric ulcer in rats.
papers.summary: Methanolic Zaghloul date palm leaf extract, rich in phenolics and 23 LC-MS-identified compounds, protected rats from ethanol-induced gastric ulcers: raising antioxidant capacity and GSH, lowering MDA, TNF-alpha, and ICAM-1, improving mucosal architecture and mucin production, and modulating E2F1, RAD21, NIBPL, and vimentin expression during mucosal repair.

papers.title: TRPML1 agonist ML-SA5 attenuates pulmonary fibroblast activation by suppressing mTOR and restoring autophagic flux.
papers.summary: The TRPML1 agonist ML-SA5 suppresses TGF-beta1-induced migration and fibrotic marker expression in human lung fibroblasts by inhibiting mTOR signaling and restoring autophagic flux. Rapamycin co-treatment enhanced the anti-fibrotic effect while an mTOR activator reversed it, positioning TRPML1 activation as a candidate pulmonary fibrosis approach.

papers.title: Characterization and phylogenetic implications of the first complete mitochondrial genome of Brachylaima sp. (Digenea: Brachylaimoidea).
papers.summary: The first complete mitochondrial genome of Brachylaima sp. (from oriental turtle dove) is 14,946 bp with 36 genes, AT-biased, with 20 canonical tRNAs and non-canonical trnS1/trnC structures. Phylogenies place it with Postharmostomum commutatum within Brachylaimidae, providing a molecular identification and comparative mitogenomics resource.

papers.title: Tetramethylpyrazine modulates the Nrf2/JNK axis to intervene in ferroptosis and neuroinflammation after spinal cord injury: an integrated perspective from antioxidant to regenerative therapy.
papers.summary: This review synthesizes tetramethylpyrazine's dual action after spinal cord injury: activating Nrf2/ARE anti-ferroptotic defense early and inhibiting JNK/AP-1-driven inflammation later, with crosstalk through ROS, TRX-1, and p62. It proposes time-sequential dual regulation, notes mechanistic and translational gaps, and frames a natural-products pathway-crosstalk paradigm.

papers.title: Syndromic Hirschsprung Disease With a Novel De Novo Sense Exonic SVA Insertion of TCF20.
papers.journal: American journal of medical genetics. Part A
papers.summary: A 40-year-old man with Hirschsprung disease, intellectual disability, and recurrent infections carried a novel de novo SVA retrotransposon insertion in TCF20 exon 2, diagnosed as TCF20-associated neurodevelopmental disorder. The case expands TAND's gastrointestinal phenotype to include aganglionosis and underscores the clinical value of transposon analysis.

papers.title: A MORC2 Variant Associated With Severe Intellectual Disability and Unusual Phenotype.
papers.journal: American journal of medical genetics. Part A
papers.summary: A 61-year-old man with the MORC2 p.Arg110Cys variant showed significant nonprogressive intellectual disability, hearing loss, retinitis pigmentosa, spasticity, and cerebellar findings beyond mild neuropathy. As the oldest reported patient with this variant, the 12-year follow-up expands MORC2's phenotypic spectrum and documents later-life progression.
